title: Finale Pilot Decision and Traffic Gates Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on deciding go/no-go for expanding pilot traffic. Reviewed latency and error trends, canary and A/B gating thresholds, agreed on runbook edits and ownership for rollback, and scheduled a short dry-run before traffic ramp. Redwood to provide revised canary dashboard and cost estimate; Vantage to run internal smoke test and confirm compliance artifact review.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-09-02 16:00 UTC | Duration 57 mins
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Marta Chen (Redwood CSM), Kellan Ortiz (Vantage VP Eng), Priya Singh (Vantage Platform Lead), Ravi Patel (Vantage SRE), Maeve O'Connor (Vantage Product)

[00:00] Lena Park: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Kellan Ortiz: Kellan here.
[00:07] Priya Singh: Priya here.
[00:08] Ravi Patel: Ravi.
[00:09] Maeve O'Connor: Maeve.
[00:10] Lena Park: And from Redwood we have Diego and Marta. Diego, do you want to kick off with a quick metric snapshot?
[00:15] Diego Morales: Yep, sure. I pulled the latest telemetry — we've got the pilot at 10% production eq, that's been running for 48 hours. Latency P50 sitting around 210ms on the hosted route, P95 around 820ms. Token cost per request trending slightly higher in the evening window because of longer-context sessions. Error rates are 0.8% at the moment, most are 5xx from a dependency timeout.
[00:40] Priya Singh: Can you repeat the 95 number? I think Priya misheard.
[00:43] Diego Morales: P95 ~820ms, sorry.
[00:45] Maeve O'Connor: That P95 is a little higher than our internal goal — we wanted under 700 for a good UX.
[00:50] Lena Park: OK noted. Two things we'll cover: the canary gating thresholds for the next traffic jump, and the A/B plan for multi-model routing. Also confirm runbook ownership and a brief dry-run.
[01:10] Kellan Ortiz: Quick question on the error spike — are those coming from Redwood side or our infra?
[01:15] Diego Morales: We traced most of the 5xx to the customer-side transform lambda timing out; there are a couple of transient GPU OOMs in the dedicated pool but those are rare. I logged both in the incident dashboard, reference id incident-72 in the runbook note.
[01:36] Ravi Patel: Yeah we saw the lambda retry pattern. We're increasing our timeout to 45s for the preprocessing step and will monitor.
[01:42] Priya Singh: What's the impact on KV cache usage if we do that? I worry about larger payloads.
[01:47] Diego Morales: KV cache — or KV cash as the transcript sometimes says — shouldn't be affected by the preprocessing timeout, it's more about prefix reuse. But bigger payloads will increase tokenization overhead, so the latency and cost go up.
[02:05] Lena Park: All right Diego, can you talk through the proposed canary thresholds and the gating rules you recommend?
[02:12] Diego Morales: Sure. Given the target SLO is 95th latency <700ms and error <0.5%, I recommended the following gate: start 5% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor P95, errors, cost per 1k tokens, and fail if P95 >800ms or errors >1.2% for a sustained 5-minute window. If that passes, move to 20% for an hour, fail if P95 increases by more than 1.5x baseline or error rate doubles. Also additional guardrail: if token cost rises >25% vs baseline, hold and alert.
[02:58] Maeve O'Connor: That 800ms threshold feels high to me — can we tighten to 750?
[03:04] Diego Morales: We can tighten, but recommend 800 for the first 5% to reduce flapping. For the 20% step we can set 750.
[03:12] Kellan Ortiz: Sounds reasonable. Are we including fallback to a lighter model if thresholds fail?
[03:17] Lena Park: Yes, the plan includes automatic fallback to the 8B quantized variant in the same family. Diego?
[03:24] Diego Morales: Correct. The routing policy will automatically use the quantized variant for that route when latency breaches or if GPU capacity drops. Note that the quantized model slightly impacts output richness; Maeve you might want to sign off on that trade-off.
[03:38] Maeve O'Connor: Right — for certain clinical language generation we prefer fidelity. We'll need A/B to preserve the fidelity checks.
[03:45] Priya Singh: How would A/B be done? 50/50? Or a targeted cohort?
[03:50] Diego Morales: For the pilot ramp we recommend targeted cohort: route 10% of users (by cookie or header) to model A (full model), 10% to model B (quantized), and 80% to current baseline for a week to compare quality and cost. Then evaluate against eval prompts in the test harness.
[04:10] Ravi Patel: Does Redwood provide eval harness? We used your open eval repo during POC but want automatic daily diffs.
[04:16] Marta Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize has the eval runner and quality regression alerts. We'll share the dashboard link and set up the daily diff for the prompt set you gave us last month.
[04:30] Maeve O'Connor: Can we also add a human-review bucket for any outputs flagged as low confidence?
[04:34] Diego Morales: You can. We'll add a webhook that tags low-confidence responses and sends to your review queue — needs a little integration on your side.
[04:43] Kellan Ortiz: On the rollout timeline, are we still aiming for traffic jump tomorrow?
[04:47] Lena Park: That's the ask from product, yes, but we wanted this sync to ensure everyone signs off on runbook and alarms.
[04:55] Priya Singh: I need the security/compliance artifact sign-off first — SOC2 doc and the VPC network diagram.
[05:02] Marta Chen: I uploaded the compliance pack to the shared drive yesterday: https://redwood.ai/s/vantage-compliance-pack. It includes SOC 2 type II summary, encryption/KMS notes, and network diagram.
[05:15] Priya Singh: Got it, will review and confirm by EOD.
[05:18] Lena Park: Great. Next, let's walk through the runbook steps for a traffic jump and rollback. Diego?
[05:25] Diego Morales: Step 0: Pre-checks — confirm capacity in Dedicated pool, model pinned version, and slot counts. Step 1: Move 5% traffic via the control plane, set runtime gate monitor. Step 2: Observe for 30 minutes. If P95 below threshold and errors stable, step up accordingly. Rollback: if we trip the gate, traffic reverts to baseline within 60 seconds and a high-priority incident page is created. Owner of rollback is the Vantage SRE on-call, but Redwood SE will assist with rapid fallback.
[05:58] Ravi Patel: Quick clarification: is rollback fully automated or manual? I want automated revert with manual confirmation.
[06:04] Diego Morales: We can do automated revert on detection and then escalate to manual confirm so the traffic doesn't oscillate — that matches your preference.
[06:12] Lena Park: Who is the primary communicator during a rollback?
[06:15] Ravi Patel: I volunteer for the immediate action as SRE. Maeve will coordinate product comms.
[06:20] Maeve O'Connor: Yep.
[06:22] Kellan Ortiz: Diego, for cost gating — if cost exceeds 25% and we hold, do we continue to route traffic to quantized model automatically to try to reduce cost?
[06:30] Diego Morales: We can do an automated traffic-shift policy: on cost gate fail, shift 60% of pilot traffic to quantized variant and keep 40% to baseline to preserve quality signals.
[06:40] Priya Singh: We need telemetry that breaks down cost per token by model variant.
[06:43] Marta Chen: That's in the per-route cost panel I'll share.
[06:47] [10:15] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[06:50] Lena Park: Now, dry-run: we propose a dry-run tomorrow at 09:30 PDT where we walk through the steps, trigger simulated alerts, and practice rollback. It's a 20-minute tabletop with the on-call SRE. Are you all available?
[07:07] Priya Singh: I can do 9:30 PDT.
[07:09] Ravi Patel: I can make that.
[07:11] Kellan Ortiz: I can join for the first 15 minutes.
[07:13] Maeve O'Connor: I'll be on for comms portion.
[07:15] Marta Chen: Redwood will run the simulated alert from the console side.
[07:19] Diego Morales: We'll create a 'simulated latency breach' event that doesn't affect real traffic but exercises the path.
[07:25] Lena Park: Good. Next: monitoring and dashboards — Priya, which critical alerts do you want created at the outset?
[07:32] Priya Singh: P95 latency >750ms sustained 5m; error rate >1% sustained 3m; cost per 1k tokens >25% baseline; model fallback trigger; mock-requests-failure rate.
[07:43] Diego Morales: We'll map those to PagerDuty and to your Slack #pilot-alerts channel.
[07:48] Kellan Ortiz: Are we logging request-level IDs that tie Redwood trace to our internal trace?
[07:52] Diego Morales: Yes, we pass back an x-request-id and you can use the trace link from the Redwood console. I will add a sample link to the runbook.
[07:59] Maeve O'Connor: On quality monitoring, what's the acceptance criteria after a week of A/B? Do we need a 95% pass rate on our eval prompts?
[08:07] Marta Chen: That's flexible. Our suggestion: model B should not regress more than 2 points on your quality metric (you provided rubric) and user-visible errors must remain under 0.5%.
[08:18] Priya Singh: Also want the regression alerts to include top 10 failing prompts so we can triage.
[08:22] Diego Morales: We'll add the top-10 failing prompt export.
[08:26] Kellan Ortiz: Any outstanding legal/procurement items before we kick?
[08:29] Marta Chen: There's a modest amendment required for the Dedicated capacity addendum; legal has the doc and you should see it in the shared drive.
[08:37] Priya Singh: We'll need to route that to procurement by EOD.
[08:40] Lena Park: Okay, let's document action items and owners.
[08:44] [08:44] Action item list begins in the transcript because Fireflies often duplicates items in-line.
[08:50] Lena Park: Diego, can you resend the canary dashboard link and the cost breakdown?
[08:54] Diego Morales: Yep will send after call.
[08:56] Priya Singh: Vantage legal will give sign-off by EOD if no surprises.
[08:59] Kellan Ortiz: I'll be available during the dry-run and will do the on-call handover notes.
[09:03] Maeve O'Connor: Product will prep the 50 prompt acceptance set used for human review.
[09:07] Diego Morales: Also I'll add a short note in the runbook about the fallback model quality caveats — sample differences and a pointer to the eval harness.
[09:18] Lena Park: any more questions?
[09:20] [09:20] Speaker 2: (background)
[09:23] Ravi Patel: One last ask — we want the ability to mute the rollout automatically at night to avoid surge from batch jobs. Can we schedule a quiet window?
[09:31] Diego Morales: Yes, you can configure traffic schedules by UTC window. We'll add a scheduled quiet window 02:00-06:00 UTC to the plan.
[09:38] Priya Singh: Great.
[09:40] Lena Park: Okay recap: dry-run tomorrow 09:30 PDT; Redwood to send canary dashboard, cost breakdown, and updated runbook with automated rollback and quiet-window config; Vantage to approve SOC2 and legal by EOD; SRE to increase preprocessing lambda timeout and confirm; product to produce prompt review set.
[09:58] Maeve O'Connor: Sounds good.
[10:00] Lena Park: If nothing else we'll close. Thanks everyone.
[10:04] Kellan Ortiz: Thanks.
[10:06] Call ended

Notes on transcript: there were a few muffled periods and one part where speaker labels dropped to generic "Speaker 1/2". Some brand names transcribed oddly (Redwood Dedikate).
